Their DS2-Instruct first makes task-informed keywords for full domain coverage. It pairs them with Bloom taxonomy levels to vary cognitive depth. Self-consistency checks then guard data quality across seven hard domains.
arxiv-2603-13532: Rudi Smith and co-authors present sketching-based methods for summing tensors in Tucker format. Compressed arithmetic on Tucker tensors must control rank growth and cost as sums are formed. Their approach avoids building large intermediate tensors and works directly on factor matrices and core tensors. Algebraic structure in Khatri-Rao and Kronecker products makes the sketching work. They analyze computational complexity and approximation properties for the method. Tests include synthetic cases, a parameter-dependent elliptic equation via GMRES, and a linear transport problem, with large savings at high accuracy.
arxiv-2603-13632: Umberto Cherubini investigates the Kelly rule when returns follow a time change process. In this broad semi-martingale setting, the rule fails to maximize the average growth rate, unless log-returns are normally distributed. Its stake is too large, and a less aggressive stake grows faster on average, he shows. A wider variance in the stochastic clock makes that failure more serious. Thorp's ruin threshold is closer, though Kelly stakes stay in the ruin-free region in his examples. A long-term acceptable investment problem follows.
arxiv-2603-13732: Hassan Jardali and co-authors introduce an LPV-MPC controller for lateral control in full-scale autonomous racing. Racing demands an optimal controller within onboard compute limits, limited track time, and high costs. Their Linear Parameter-Varying Model Predictive Controller ran on an IAC AV-24 race car. It achieved stable performance at speeds over 160 mph in their final race run. The authors detail controller design, model parameter extraction, and system-level implementation choices. A Python implementation of the framework is publicly available.
arxiv-2603-13832: Ruan and co-authors improve how robots plan dexterous grasps with many fingers. A good grasp must be varied, free of collisions, and stable under contact forces. Their method, GraspADMM, keeps the wide sampling of the Dexonomy framework but refines grasps with ADMM optimization. The split lets target contact points on the object move to raise stability scores. The hand pose then adjusts to reach those points without penetration. This pairing aims to keep diversity while fixing weak points of each older approach.
arxiv-2603-14232: Zhang and co-authors present S2GS, a streaming method that rebuilds and understands 3D scenes frame by frame. Offline methods redo global math over all past frames, so cost balloons on long streams. S2GS never looks ahead and never reworks old frames. A geometry branch updates Gaussian scene elements step by step. A semantic branch, fed by a 2D vision model, adds masks and identity codes for objects. Tests match strong offline systems while scaling past 1,000 frames.
arxiv-2603-14532: Kim and Jeong test how confined bacteria sort themselves under an oxygen gradient. Aerotactic bacteria swim in a thin liquid film between two solid plates. Oxygen enters from one side only. At low density, cells gather at both walls in a symmetric pattern. At high density, cells shift toward the oxygen side. The shift comes from a self-made gradient, as dense cells breathe oxygen down. A diffusion-advection model with wall attraction matches the lab data well, they report.
arxiv-2603-14632: Benjamin, Jain and Nandakumar detect synthetic fingerprints under continual few-shot adaptation. Generative models now fake fingerprints well enough to threaten scanners. Injected fakes can slip into enrollment or login steps. A fixed detector overfits its training fakes and misses new generators. Their setup treats each new fake style as a small-shot update task. Cross-entropy and contrastive losses train the features. A few old-style samples replay during tuning to curb forgetting. Tests span several network backbones and generator types.
arxiv-2603-14832: Yang and co-authors mix 2.5D and 3D models for COVID-19 diagnosis from chest CT scans. Slice views and full volumes carry complementary signal. The 2.5D branch reads axial, coronal and sagittal slices with a DINOv3 transformer. The 3D branch uses ResNet-18 over volumes for spatial context. Variance risk training plus contrastive steps harden the 3D branch across sources. Logit-level ensembling joins both verdicts. Binary detection hits 94.48% accuracy on the PHAROS-AIF-MIH bench, they report. The slice model alone leads multi-class disease sorting.
arxiv-2603-14932: Li, Deng and Zhang extend the consistent-Q scheme to odd-odd nuclei inside an algebraic boson model. Odd-odd systems challenge theory more than even-even ones. The interacting boson fermion fermion model frames their low-lying states. Consistent-Q mapping charts nuclear shape phase diagrams in that frame. Unpaired nucleons join the picture in this extension. Critical behavior survives their presence across three shape transitions, they find. Shape transitions thus steer odd-odd structure in heavy mass regions. Level evolution follows the same phase logic.
arxiv-2603-15132: Wang and co-authors present WiT, a pixel-space image generator that adds semantic waypoints to ease trajectory conflict. Flow matching models that work on raw pixels lack clear semantic structure. Transport paths for different targets can clash and slow learning. WiT projects compact waypoints from pretrained vision features to guide the flow. A light predictor infers the waypoint from the current noisy state during sampling. On ImageNet 2012, WiT beat strong pixel-space baselines across model scales, reaching an FID of 1.79 at the largest size.
arxiv-2603-15232: Charpentier and Fernandes Machado split the score of a probabilistic forecast into clear parts. A forecast can be well calibrated only if it keeps enough of the input data. Their formulas make that link exact for any proper loss. Expected loss breaks into a regret part, tied to poor calibration, and an entropy part for what stays unknown. For classification, a third part prices the data lost when raw features shrink to one score. The work also covers recalibration, model merging, and boosting.
arxiv-2603-15332: Scarpa and co-authors calibrate spectral siren cosmology with synthetic catalogs of binary black hole mergers. Gravitational wave events give distance directly, but redshift hides inside the source masses. A flow-based pipeline fits population models to mock catalogs built from physical formation recipes. The mock data mix isolated binaries and pairs formed in dense star clusters. The B-POP catalog fits the mass and redshift spread of GWTC-4.0 events well. They also find that the inferred Hubble constant trades off against the share of pairs from each channel.
arxiv-2603-15432: Meng and co-authors release Gym-V, a shared platform of visual environments for training vision agents with reinforcement learning. It holds 179 procedurally generated environments across ten domains, with adjustable difficulty. Using it, they find that observation scaffolding decides training success more than the learning algorithm. Captions and stated game rules can make or break learning. Broad training across task types transferred well, while narrow training sometimes hurt. Multi-turn interaction magnified every one of these effects.
arxiv-2603-15532: Hoang and Nguyen give a formula for the separation Lojasiewicz exponents of two real analytic set germs in the plane. These exponents gauge how sharply two sets pull apart near a shared point. Their formula reads the exponents off the Newton-Puiseux expansions of the functions that define the sets. For two real algebraic sets, they add an effective exponent bound stated through the degrees. The result turns an abstract quantity into a computable one.
arxiv-2603-15632: Boumali and Jafari study a three-dimensional Dirac oscillator under deformed relativity rules. Doubly Special Relativity adds an invariant high-energy scale beside the speed of light. They build an exactly solvable model with a linear momentum coupling. Two classic DSR forms and a generalized Planck-length form are tested. The wave functions keep their oscillator shape in all cases. Energy levels shift by branch, and the shifts grow with excitation. The plain limit returns smoothly as the scale grows.
arxiv-2603-15832: Kang revisits the prices-versus-quantities choice under deep uncertainty. A regulator picks among all nonlinear price schedules for best worst-case welfare. Known inputs are preference spreads and the mean marginal externality. The joint pattern linking tastes to harm stays unknown. The best robust policy turns out to be a quantity control. Positive externalities call for a floor, negative ones for a ceiling. One extra fact can flip the answer to a flat tax. The result grounds simple rules in welfare terms.
arxiv-2603-15932: Song and co-authors synthesize future lung scans to speed cancer calls. Unclear low-dose CT findings force waits of up to a year. Their NAMD diffusion model paints a one-year follow-up nodule image. Inputs blend the baseline scan, nodule biomarkers, and health record data. A nodule-aligned latent space ties image gaps to biomarker change. An LLM encodes the mixed record data for conditioning. On NLST data, malignancy calls hit an AUROC of 0.805. The method beats plain baseline scans and rival generators.
arxiv-2603-16132: Jana and co-authors squeeze two honeycomb magnetoelectrics to watch structure shift. Mn4Nb2O9 and Mn4Ta2O9 share a layered honeycomb frame. Raman spectra, synchrotron diffraction, and DFT track the squeeze. The tantalum form breaks local symmetry at just 0.5 GPa. More quiet transitions follow near 3.2, 6, and 10 GPa. A long-range phase change starts near 14 GPa there. The niobium form mirrors the pattern at shifted pressures. Both end in mixed phases that coexist past 26 GPa. Uneven axis squeeze may boost interlayer magnetic coupling.
arxiv-2603-16432: Khanbayov and co-authors benchmark tools that recover physics from plain video. No shared real-world test existed for this task. Prior sets were synthetic or limited to single bodies. Their IRIS set holds 240 real videos at 4K and 60 frames per second. Each video pairs with measured ground-truth parameters and governing equations. A standard protocol scores accuracy, robustness, and equation choice. Baselines expose steady failure modes for future work.
arxiv-2603-16532: Dey and Faizal trace quartic changes to dispersion relations back to geometry. Such changes are Planck-scale guesses in quantum gravity work. Their claim is that the quartic form arises generically. It appears when phase space carries a symplectic structure and a matching complex one. A single geometric length scale then sets the correction. Three routes confirm the same result. They use Fedosov-Berezin quantization, spectral geometry, and a topos approach.
arxiv-2603-16632: Abanto-Leon and Maghsudi manage radio resources for systems that sense and communicate at once. They jointly tune time slots, beams, function choice, and user-target pairing. Real channels carry flaws from motion, delays, and hardware limits. The goal is to cut energy and time use, with time saved first. The raw problem is a hard nonconvex mixed-integer program. Hidden convex structure allows an exact semidefinite rewrite. That form solves to global optimality. Simulations show gains up to 88% over baselines.
arxiv-2603-16732: Zhu and co-authors target worst-class errors in long-tailed recognition. A few head classes dominate real image data; many tail classes stay tiny. Feature learning then tilts toward the head, and rare classes suffer. Their bound ties worst-class error to a confusion matrix's spectral norm. That insight yields the CAR regularizer, trained to shrink that norm. A differentiable surrogate keeps the estimate smooth across batches. Across ImageNet-LT and other benchmarks, worst-class accuracy rose. Gains held both from scratch and from pretrained starts.
arxiv-2603-16932: Shabtay and co-authors present AwaRes, a framework that lets vision language models fetch fine image detail only when needed. Full high resolution input is costly, while low resolution input can miss small text. AwaRes starts from a low resolution global view. A tool call then retrieves high resolution crops for the parts a query needs. Training data are built with a judge that labels when cropping helps, plus an oracle that locates the evidence. Training mixes supervised fine tuning with GRPO and a reward that charges for crops.
arxiv-2603-17332: Kamada proves new identities that express powers of positive integers through multinomial coefficients. Such coefficients generalize the binomial ones to splits into several parts. The identities here do not come from the two standard sources for such formulas. They arise neither from the multinomial theorem nor from the multinomial Vandermonde convolution. The paper presents the identities and proves them. The proofs are short and use counting steps that any reader can check.
arxiv-2603-17632: Bartels, Lahr, Carron, and Zeilinger make Gaussian process learning fast enough for real-time control. Model predictive control gains from GP models of residual dynamics, plus their uncertainty. Full GP updates cost too much for live loops, though. Their spatio-temporal approximation learns online at constant cost per step. It tracks time-varying systems as they drift. Tests in simulation and on a real miniature race car show gains.
arxiv-2603-17832: Hernandez and co-authors test whether language models can stage a play from prose alone. The task asks for scenes, speaker spots, moves, and room types from text with no spatial cues. A dramaturgy-based scoring suite grades the outputs in a fixed way. Training mixes rejection fine-tuning with rewards that software can verify. On classic English texts, layout quality rose across several metrics, they report. Human judges and an LLM judge both liked the gains.
arxiv-2603-18132: Batell and co-authors show how thermal misalignment can phase out dark matter isocurvature. Weak links to the thermal bath push a scalar field to large values early on. The relic amount then rests on masses and couplings, not the starting field value. Inflation still gives the light field uncorrelated fluctuations that source isocurvature. A late-time phase offset between the zero mode and long waves cuts the final density contrast.
arxiv-2603-18332: Fairman and co-authors present the first atmospheric study of the aligned hot Jupiter NGTS-2b with JWST. One NIRSpec/G395H transit covers 2.84 to 5.18 microns for this 1468 K planet. Weak water and carbon dioxide features fit high mean molecular weight solutions. Some solutions exceed interior model limits, pointing to cloud-metallicity degeneracy and prior bias. Equilibrium retrievals hint at subsolar carbon-to-oxygen ratio and supersolar metallicity, with wide ranges.
arxiv-2603-18532: Choi and co-authors fine-tune robot vision-language-action models inside worlds built by generative 3D models. A language-driven designer creates 100 varied scenes with new objects and backgrounds. Training across these scenes lifts simulation success from 9.7 percent to 79.8 percent. Tasks also finish faster. The trained policy then moves to a real robot, where success rises from 21.7 percent to 75 percent. Tests with more scenes show that scene variety drives better zero-shot generalization.
arxiv-2603-18632: Ferrera and co-authors measure single-particle strength in the neutron-rich isotope calcium-51. A calcium-50 beam struck a deuterium target in inverse kinematics at RIBF. Missing mass spectra gave excited state energies up to 4.2 MeV. Proton angle patterns yielded cross sections for each state. Comparison with distorted wave calculations produced spectroscopic factors. The data support spin assignments for two negative parity states. They also hint at a 9/2+ state tied to neutron excitation into the g9/2 orbital, which constrains shell evolution models.
arxiv-2603-18832: Estienne gives a new proof of a 2007 theorem by Papanikolas on Carlitz logarithms. The theorem links linear and algebraic independence for these function-field logarithms. Papanikolas used t-motives in the first proof. Estienne uses Mahler's method instead. The proof revisits and extends Denis's 2006 approach, which handled logarithms of elements of Fq(theta) through a Mahler system. The new route shows Mahler systems can carry the full result. It offers a second road into algebraic independence questions in the Carlitz setting.
arxiv-2603-19232: Wang and co-authors make images from discrete tokens that carry far more detail than usual. Most such tokens hold 8 to 32 numbers, which drops rich meaning. Their CubiD model works on tokens with up to about 1,000 numbers. Any entry at any spot can be masked and then predicted from the rest. The step count stays fixed no matter how large the tokens grow. On ImageNet it leads its class and scales to 3.7 billion weights. The same tokens still serve image grasp tasks.
arxiv-2603-19332: Ammar builds quaternionic versions of the core tools of Nevanlinna value distribution theory. That theory tracks how often a meromorphic function takes each value. Starting from a Jensen formula for quaternions, he defines a total order and a counting function. He adds Weil functions and mean proximity functions in the same setting. A new class of balanced functions covers slice-preserving and most semiregular cases. A harmonic remainder term fixes a defect in the Jensen formula. He proves a full first main theorem for the balanced class.
arxiv-2603-19432: The MMGPDs Collaboration studies how parton distribution inputs shape generalized parton distributions. Six global fits are run with three modern PDF sets at three scales and varied orders. Wide elastic electron scattering data pin the results across momentum transfer. The best fit uses NNPDF40 inputs at next-to-leading order overall. Choice of PDF set matters most at low momentum transfer. The order of the calculation has a mild effect on the outcome. Extracted proton radii shift by real amounts between the fit sets.
arxiv-2603-19532: Ben Tamo and co-authors present EvidenceRL, a training method that keeps language model answers tied to evidence. Models often give fluent answers that no source supports. EvidenceRL scores each answer for grounding in retrieved evidence and for correctness. Group Relative Policy Optimization then trains the generator on those scores. On cardiac diagnosis, grounding rose sharply and hallucinations fell nearly fivefold. On legal reasoning, faithfulness more than doubled on one model. Accuracy held up in both domains.
arxiv-2603-20032: Staszewski and Borówko simulate surfactant solutions squeezed into narrow slit pores. They study a nonionic surfactant in water, both in bulk and in confinement. Pores have either matching walls or Janus-like pairs with unlike faces. Each wall can be inert, water-loving, or water-hating. The team focuses on the shapes the surfactants form inside each slit. Pore type and width both steer the outcome. In slits, the surfactants build structures that never appear in the bulk. Adsorption happens in aggregated patches rather than smooth layers.
arxiv-2603-20332: Macaia and co-authors lay out a step-by-step framework for modeling indoor wireless signals. Reflections, diffraction, and material effects make indoor propagation hard to predict. Yet over 80% of wireless data is used indoors, so accuracy matters. Their simulations use Wireless Insite ray tracing for a full department floor. SketchUp builds the layout from field measures, and MATLAB plots channel outputs. They test several transmitter and receiver spots for cases like coverage holes.
arxiv-2603-20532: Dinsmore and Romani model the thin X-ray filaments that trail some pulsars. These nebulae sit at an angle to the pulsar's motion. They argue that cosmic ray driven turbulence does the key work. It scatters the electron pairs and guides their flow along the filament. No highly amplified magnetic fields are needed in this picture. A simulation built on it matches images and spectra of the three best measured filaments. Many particles escape the filament in the model. They may add a large share to the local positron flux.
arxiv-2603-20732: Lombard and co-authors release MzansiText and MzansiLM for South African languages. The corpus supports all eleven official written languages, nine of them low resource. MzansiLM is a 125 million parameter model trained from scratch. They test three ways to adapt it to new tasks. Single language tuning hit 20.65 BLEU on isiXhosa data to text work. That rivals models ten times larger. Mixed language tuning helped topic sorting for close languages. Few shot reasoning stayed near chance at this size.
arxiv-2603-21132: Li and co-authors compute light-cone distribution amplitudes of vector mesons in a self-consistent light-front quark model. They cover twist-2 and twist-3 amplitudes, plus Gegenbauer, longitudinal, and transverse moments. Model parameters are fixed by meson decay constants. Flavor symmetry breaking shows up more strongly in the twist-3 amplitudes. In the heavy quark limit, twist dependence fades, and the amplitudes of pseudoscalar and vector mesons with the same quarks converge. The team reads this as an approximate spin and twist independence pattern in that limit.
arxiv-2603-21632: Lee and co-authors report field trials of extreme MIMO wireless in the 7 gigahertz band, a candidate spectrum for 6G. The band balances coverage and capacity, but needs far stronger beamforming than current 5G gear. They study a 256-port base station and user device setup, first in simulation, then as a working prototype. Urban outdoor trials achieved eight-layer downlink MIMO over 100 megahertz, passing 3 gigabits per second to one user. Channel measurements suggest the large aperture supports high-order multiplexing even with few angular clusters.
arxiv-2603-21932: Bizzarri models trade between firms in a production network as a web of double auctions. Each firm holds market power on both sides: it can move prices for its inputs and its outputs at once. The size and split of surplus follow only from technology, network position, and consumer tastes. The usual shortcut, treating firms as price takers when buying inputs, distorts the picture. It understates final prices and overstates the surplus that flows upstream. Those biases carry into predictions about how mergers affect welfare, Bizzarri shows.
arxiv-2603-22332: Mangussi and co-authors benchmark language models as fillers of missing table values. The study tests five large language models against six top classic methods. It spans 29 datasets and three missingness patterns, with up to a fifth of values gone. Top models like Gemini and Claude beat classic methods on real datasets. On synthetic data, the classic MICE method wins instead. The authors link the model edge to prior exposure to like data in pre-training. The trade-off is cost: model imputation runs slower and pricier.
arxiv-2603-22432: Efthymiou and Zampetakis study how fast Glauber dynamics samples from spin-glass models on sparse random graphs. Their focus is the two-spin model, whose Gaussian couplings make the interactions unbounded and hard to analyze. They show the mixing time stays near-linear in the number of vertices at low enough temperature. The proof uses stochastic localization, a tool not used before for diluted spin glasses. The same ideas also speed up sampling for the bounded Viana-Bray model.
arxiv-2603-22532: Webster and co-authors benchmark methods for finding the distance of quantum and classical codes. A code's distance measures how well it detects errors, so it sets the code's strength. For quantum low-density codes the value is hard to compute, and circuit-level distance is harder still. The team compares exact methods, like SAT and integer programming, with faster heuristics that only bound the answer. Their own evolved search method, QDistEvol, performs well on the quantum codes tested. All tools ship in a public Python package.
arxiv-2603-22632: Qu and co-authors report an experiment on a driven phonon mode in a quantum material. They ask whether driven, energy-losing systems can still follow a thermodynamic account. Past a threshold drive strength, the phonon mode shows a delayed ultrafast response. The authors link that delay to excitations spreading across many phonon levels. Lindblad dynamics fitted to the data support this view. Trajectories for three drive settings fall on one shared surface, set by energy and coherence together. The result frames a coherence-extended thermodynamic regime.
arxiv-2603-22732: Nguyen and Park present SOUPLE, a method to find and segment the source of a sound in an image. It builds on the CLIP image-text model. Fixed text prompts link poorly with audio tokens, they note. SOUPLE swaps fixed prompts for learnable context tokens. Those tokens use visual features to build context for a mask decoder. Tests on VGGSound, SoundNet, and AVSBench show better localization and segmentation scores. The method bridges the semantic gap between audio and visual inputs.
arxiv-2603-22932: González, Ramos Pérez, and Rodríguez Raposo study modules over a Hopf brace. A Hopf brace pairs two Hopf structures in a symmetric monoidal category. The authors prove the module category over the brace matches a known category. It is isomorphic to modules over the smash product algebra of the two parts. They also characterize modules in Zhu's sense. That class is singled out by where a certain action sits: the cocommutativity class of the second part.
arxiv-2603-23132: Pan and co-authors present InterDyad, a framework for two-person speech-to-video generation. Prior methods miss how partners react to each other. Their system queries structural motion guidance to shape reactions. An Interactivity Injector reenacts video from identity-free motion priors. A query-based alignment step bridges speech and those priors. A language model reads intent from audio to time the reactions. Role-aware Gaussian guidance improves lip sync under hard head poses. New metrics score dyadic interaction quality. Tests beat prior top methods on natural interaction.
arxiv-2603-23332: Frenkel and Martins-Filho examine how the effective action of quantum gravity depends on gauge choice. They study gravity coupled to matter fields in a general background gauge. Their off-shell result at one loop is explicit. In one special gauge it shrinks to the classic 't Hooft-Veltman action. They confirm the DeWitt-Kallosh theorem, which says the on-shell action must not depend on the gauge parameter. They then wield that theorem to expose the theory's non-renormalizability in a general gauge.
arxiv-2603-23532: Nimmagadda and four co-authors test whether tree-shaped JSON can hold the meaning of science sentences. They fine-tune a small language model with a new structural loss. The model turns each sentence into a layered JSON tree. A second model then rebuilds the sentence from that tree alone. The team compare the rebuild with the source by meaning and wording overlap. The match stays strong, which shows the format keeps the facts well. Such trees could help machines store and search science text.
arxiv-2603-23732: Olver builds polynomial bases that mirror the de Rham complex on disks and cylinders. The bases respect spin symmetry and the rim conditions of each shape. He starts from vector and matrix polynomials on the unit disk, kin to the Zernike family. A matrix weight then forces vector fields to sit normal at the rim. Gradients and curls of the new family land on known Zernike forms. In cylinders, plain recurrences link gradient, curl, and divergence. The whole complex splits into small exact blocks.
arxiv-2603-23832: Kulikov and Larsen study eigenvalue counts for localization operators built from Fourier transforms and set projections. They count how many eigenvalues fall in a middle band as one set grows large. For sets made of finitely many boxes, they prove a sharp uniform bound. For general sets, their bound sits one logarithm above the guessed best bound. They apply the results to trace estimates for rough functions. One payoff is an enhanced area law in the box case.
arxiv-2603-24032: Wu and co-authors study how the path taken around exceptional points shapes state transfer and sensing. Exceptional points in non-Hermitian systems promise sharp sensitivity and chiral transfer. They test three time-modulated loops in a two-level system. Loops that avoid the point give robust symmetric transfer. Loops that circle it give chiral transfer, with robustness set by distance and direction. Path design also tunes sensor strength, time window, and selectivity. Eigenstate-based sensing reaches full parameter selectivity, which eigenvalue methods cannot.
arxiv-2603-24332: Galinier and co-authors search the main belt for asteroids that match the meteorite Erg Chech 002. This andesitic meteorite likely came from the crust of an early differentiated planetesimal. A past Gaia study flagged 142 candidate analogues. The authors observe 20 of them with NASA's IRTF in the near-infrared. None of the 20 matches the meteorite. Most classify as V-types. Two asteroids from earlier work do match its spectrum well, and a third remains possible. These bodies may form a new class of andesitic asteroids.
arxiv-2603-24732: Mishra studies confinement in holographic theories at a finite vacuum angle, theta. A five-dimensional setup models the effect with a bulk scalar. Its boundary conditions come from higher-dimensional examples. In the small backreaction limit, the temperature for the transition falls quadratically with theta, matching lattice results. The susceptibility also drops sharply across the transition, again matching the lattice. The transition rate grows or shrinks with theta. Which way it goes depends on whether the theory's high-energy deformation is relevant or irrelevant.
arxiv-2603-24832: Ballu and co-authors study soliton turbulence in a strongly driven one-dimensional Bose gas. A periodically oscillating linear potential drives the weakly interacting gas. After a transient, the gas reaches a quasi-steady state holding several solitons. At weak drive, the solitons barely disturb each other. At strong drive, they intertwine in a regime akin to turbulence. The momentum distribution marks both regimes, with distinct power-law decays at weak and strong drive. Inverse scattering analysis tracks the solitons in each regime.
arxiv-2603-24932: Chen and co-authors study the identification between bulk and boundary charges in gravity. Using the Wald formalism, they consider perturbations from a generic non-electromagnetic matter field. The identification was known on asymptotically flat stationary spacetimes. They show it also holds on asymptotically anti-de Sitter stationary spacetimes. The result further reduces to the usual form for a test point particle. That case appears as the limiting case of general matter, tying the abstract identity to a concrete physical picture.
arxiv-2603-25432: Rock defines pixelation, a new kind of localization meant as a loose approximation tool. A path category is built from a set, chosen paths into it, and a sameness rule on paths. A screen is a partition that respects those paths. For a ring, the paths can also be weighted by modules and cut down by an ideal. Pixelation localizes at a screen, and the result mimics the source category. Uses include a fresh view of the Zariski topology and a broad form of higher Auslander algebras.
arxiv-2603-25832: Ilin and Hu present a neural particle method for simulating collisional plasmas. Their target is the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau system, which tracks phase-space flow with Landau collisions. A recent particle method estimates the velocity score with a blob scheme at quadratic cost. Their method trains a neural network on the fly to estimate the score, at linear cost. They prove the scheme keeps momentum and energy and lowers an entropy estimate. On three classic tests, it beats the blob method in accuracy and runs faster with less memory.
arxiv-2603-25932: Gao, Zhang, and Chen survey students on what they think of faculty using generative AI. Research so far has mostly policed student use of these tools. The team analyzed replies from 156 undergraduate and graduate students. They sorted students into four camps, from optimists to non-supporters. Thirty-seven percent opposed use by both students and faculty. Thirty-one percent backed use in both cases. Most students, 79 percent, doubted the validity of AI answers. Many feared a futile cycle in which faculty lean on AI and think less deeply.
arxiv-2603-26032: Batan Arachchige and co-authors present a way to scrub private data from prompts sent to remote language models. Their method perturbs each character of a prompt at random, under differential privacy rules. The remote model first restores the text, then does the asked task. Common words survive the noise because context guides the repair. Rare sensitive words, like names, are hard to rebuild. Tests on health and email data bear this out. Private items come back at near-chance rates.
arxiv-2603-26132: Ishikawa and co-authors show that the structure of a liquid can decide which species join a growing crystal. Textbook views treat stable multicomponent crystals as near-random solid solutions. Their simulations use a rocksalt-type model of AgPbBiTe3. High-valence cations form liquid clusters that already match the crystal pattern. They attach to the growth front with ease. Low-valence cations sit in messier liquid sites and attach poorly. Growth thus turns species-selective and slows down. Lab spectra find extra silver near surfaces and grain edges, as predicted.
arxiv-2603-26332: Jung, Yoon, and Cho present CALRK-Bench, a test of legal reasoning built on Korean law. Legal judgment needs more than rule use; the setting around a rule matters too. The bench checks whether models can spot when a norm holds in time, judge if case facts suffice, and explain shifts in verdicts. Its cases come from precedents and consultation records, checked by legal experts. Even recent large models score low on all three tasks.
arxiv-2603-26632: Vieira, Vitorino, Maia, and Praça test how well malware detectors transfer across datasets with mismatched features. Public malware datasets rarely share the same feature sets, which blocks reuse of trained models. Their pipeline unifies EMBERv2 features and trains paired models on two data mixes. The models are then scored on TRITIUM, INFERNO, and the large SOREL-20M set. The study weighs which preprocessing choices keep detection strong when the data shifts, a key need as obfuscation keeps evolving.
arxiv-2603-26732: Kikawa and co-authors build a semi-automatic system to screen plastic scintillator cubes for future neutrino detectors. Large detectors need millions of near-identical parts, so checks must be exact and fast. A motorised stage turns each one-centimetre cube before six high-grade cameras. Software measures size, surface bumps, and the holes meant for light-guide fibres, then sorts each cube as pass or fail. The prototype hits 10 micrometre precision and agrees with manual checks over 80% of the time, with a 3.1% rejection rate.
arxiv-2603-26932: Lvov and Van Werde ask how often a graph is pinned down by spectral data alone. They give the first sharp conjectures on how often two sufficient conditions hold. Their framework recasts the conditions with modules over polynomial rings tied to the adjacency matrix. Random matrix ensembles over profinite completions make the module spread tractable. One condition needs the walk matrix determinant to be square-free. The other uses the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial. The method turns a graph question into module statistics.
arxiv-2603-27032: Palaisti introduces asymptotic universal Koszulity for a class of graded-commutative algebras. The idea: an infinite algebra is built up from finite-type quadratic subalgebras that are universally Koszul. Palaisti shows the class is stable under colimits, products, and base change. A local test checks the trait on finite pieces of degree one. In Galois cohomology, a colimit theorem covers pro-p groups in a broad setting. Rings then arise as colimits of finite quotients. Patching ideas point toward number-theory uses of the setup.
arxiv-2603-27132: Lau and co-authors propose diffusive tides as a source of irregular repeating tidal disruptions. A star passing a massive black hole usually must skim the tidal radius to lose mass. Here, a wider binary builds tidal strain slowly across many orbits instead. The accumulated perturbation can trigger a nonlinear instability that ejects mass. That produces repeated eruptions with widely varying gaps between them. The mechanism works for white dwarfs or main-sequence stars at a few tidal radii. It requires orbital periods shorter than the tidal dissipation timescale.
arxiv-2603-27432: Chun studies how two common scaling steps shape neural network complexity. LayerNorm centers data onto a flat plane through the origin. RMSNorm instead projects data onto a sphere. He proves the flat step cuts a complexity measure by exactly half the output size. The curved step leaves that measure intact. Any bend, however small, blocks the drop. Tests with a single-layer setup match both claims. Softmax data can trigger the same drop through a hidden bias.
arxiv-2603-27632: Le and Zhi give robots maps that also flag where data are missing. ContraMap adds an explicit uncertainty class to kernel maps. Synthetic noise samples train that extra class. Unseen zones then read as a contrastive class. Maps and doubt estimates come out jointly in real time. No Bayesian inference is needed at runtime. Tests cover 2D occupancy and 3D semantic mapping. Tabletop reconstruction also works well. Speed beats Bayesian kernel baselines by far.
arxiv-2603-27932: Lan and Pan prove vanishing results for Shimura variety cohomology. Completed cohomology gathers deep arithmetic information. An almost Kodaira-type result in mixed traits anchors the proof. That input comes from Bhatt's recent work. Regular infinitesimal weights then face a tight constraint. They can appear only in the middle degree. The setting is the locally analytic completed theory. General Shimura varieties are covered.
arxiv-2603-28232: The BESIII Collaboration reports the first observation of the charmed baryon decay Lambda_c+ to a neutron, a pion, and an eta meson. The team analyzed 6.1 inverse femtobarns of collision data from the BEPCII collider. The decay shows up at 9.5 sigma significance. Its branching fraction comes out near 2.94 thousandths, measured against a known sister decay. A search for the same decay through an a0(980)+ intermediate state found no signal, so the team sets an upper limit.
arxiv-2603-28332: Wang and four co-authors give a quantum algorithm for adversarial training, the costly defense that hardens machine learning models against attack. Each update first needs a fresh attack on the current model, which gets pricey at scale. The team rewrites the attacker-learner loop as a large sparse linear system whose last block holds the trained weights. Under stability and sparsity assumptions, the query cost grows gently with model size. The work puts AI security training on firmer quantum ground.
arxiv-2603-28732: Yu and co-authors present Pandora, a system that builds articulated 3D scene graphs from egocentric vision. Robot maps inherit the robot's own limits, so drawers and cabinets may stay unexplored. Pandora uses video from a human wearing Project Aria glasses while exploring a scene. Simple heuristics recover models of articulated object parts from that data. The models join a 3D scene graph capturing object dynamics and container relations. A Boston Dynamics Spot robot used the graph to retrieve hidden target items, matching strong methods that use other inputs.
arxiv-2603-29332: Wei and co-authors introduce MS-Emulator, a framework that reproduces whole-body human motion with a muscle-driven model. Muscle activity cannot be measured directly inside the body. Inverse dynamics tools struggle with redundant control in such a large system. Their framework runs large-scale GPU simulation in parallel. Adversarial reward pooling and value-guided flow search ease the training. The model drives about 700 muscles. It matched joint angles well on dance, cartwheel, and backflip tasks. It also found distinct control policies with near-identical outer motion.
arxiv-2603-29532: Olucha and co-authors present a Bayesian way to learn linear parameter-varying models with doubt bounds. Such surrogate models help analyze and control complex nonlinear systems. Past data-driven methods give no uncertainty for the model itself. Without it, users cannot tell when the model leaves its training range. Their method fits the model and its scheduling map jointly. It reports confidence bounds on predicted responses from raw input-output data. Both sensor noise and limited-data doubt are counted. A mass-spring-damper test case shows the approach.
arxiv-2603-29632: Shen and co-authors compare ways for AI agents to collaborate on automated research. Single models hit cognitive limits, so teams are gaining ground. Their testbed runs controlled experiments with worktree isolation and shared memory. A single agent faces two team designs under fixed time budgets. Subagents explore in parallel and merge results afterward. Agent teams hand off work between experts before running code. Subagent mode proved sturdy and fast for broad, shallow searches. Teams aligned theory better but broke more often in operation.
arxiv-2603-30032: Tuttösí and co-authors test whether targeted speech timing, not global slowing, aids comprehension. Talkers often slow all speech for struggling listeners, with unclear benefit. Machine speech now allows precise rate control for experiments. Reverse-correlation tests reveal a scissor-like timing pattern around a target vowel contrast. That pattern stays stable across native and non-native listener groups. Using it helps second-language listeners and natives in noise. A text-to-speech tool now copies the pattern. Listeners gain without noticing the change.
arxiv-2604-00132: Bai and Johansen build a machine-learning stand-in for Maxwell's equations along a line where waves meet a material boundary. Training data come from detailed finite-volume runs with varied starting states and varied light speed in one material. A vision-transformer design learns physical and frequency embeddings together, with Fourier transforms in its latent space. Wave-number spectra match the runs closely, and relative errors stay below 10 percent across more than 75 rollout steps despite the sharp edge.
arxiv-2604-00932: Dey and team present Eigen-CG inequalities for nonconvex tuning problems, got by applying Chvátal-Gomory rounding to eigenvector bounds. They define three nested groups, prove they nest strictly, and show the convex conic closure of two of them equals the Boros-Hammer inequalities, which include triangle and McCormick inequalities. Dense Eigen-CG cuts prove weak with the standard SDP-plus-McCormick relaxation, so the team builds a plan to find sparse cuts. Sparse cuts beyond triangle ones improve dual bounds a lot.
arxiv-2604-01032: Aadi and team generate sub-metre lunar elevation models from Chandrayaan-2 Orbiter High Resolution Camera images with an open-source pipeline. They pick likely stereo pairs from non-paired archives via archive geometry. Dense stereo matching and ray tracing build point clouds, gridded into models at 24 to 54 cm detail across five lunar sites. Elevation match comes from Iterative Closest Point matching against Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter terrain models plus offset fix. Checks give height RMSE 5.85 m at native detail and flat error within about 30 cm.
arxiv-2604-01332: Kuehnert and colleagues ask whether vendor self-reports actually help governments vet artificial intelligence, studying the GovAI Coalition FactSheet through interviews and a systematic read of completed sheets. They find one document pulled three ways at once: advertising the product, supporting due diligence, and opening early dialogue between buyer and seller. Voluntary public disclosure plus those clashing aims stop FactSheets working alone as evaluation or risk tools. Treated instead as trust-building records, the authors argue, they can still support better disclosure and governance over time.
arxiv-2604-01532: Li and colleagues introduce PHMForge, a test bed closing three mix-ups: rule skill with reasoning, tool faults with agent faults, and tool use with tool lookup. PHMForge ships 99 expert scenarios across eight asset classes, served through 39 MCP-native tools wrapping PHM methods. Across three agent setups and six model bases, the best setup reaches 80.8 percent pass at 1, with gaps in planning and tool order errors. Using text lookup in place of MCP runs drops Remaining Useful Life pass-all-3 from 100 percent to 20 percent on the battery class.
arxiv-2604-01632: Freeburg shows a single axiom — hierarchical symmetry — is necessary and sufficient for the cascade multiplier to be log-Poisson. He proves a characterization theorem giving the log-Poisson law explicitly. A classification theorem places the log-Poisson class inside the log-infinitely-divisible family. A stability theorem gives sharp constants: square root of one plus beta when the limiting increment is known, square root of two when fit. An unconditional propagation theorem transfers the bound to the multiplier distribution at rate square root of epsilon, with a matching bound.
arxiv-2604-01732: Tuyen Van Kieu and colleagues tackle cutting rectangles from stock sheets to meet demand, minimizing waste. Demand expansion causes a combinatorial blow-up. Their SAT framework assigns each copy to a sheet and applies non-overlap constraints only within a sheet. To minimize sheet count they compare non-incremental SAT, incremental SAT, and weighted partial MaxSAT. On Cui-Zhao benchmarks their best setups certify two to three times as many instances as provably optimal than OR-Tools, CPLEX and Gurobi, with the ranking depending on rotation.
arxiv-2604-01832: Rong and colleagues present GAP-URGENet, a fusion framework built for the ICASSP 2026 URGENT Challenge's first track. A generative branch restores speech fully in a self-supervised domain and rebuilds the waveform with a neural vocoder, while a predictive branch enhances spectrograms for complementary cues. Both branches' outputs are combined by a post-processing module, which also extends bandwidth to 48 kHz, later downsampled to the source rate. The fusion improves robustness and perceptual quality, topping blind-test scores and ranking first on objective scores.
arxiv-2604-01932: Pio-Lopez, Hartl and Levin introduce BraiNCA, a brain-style neural cellular automaton breaking the grid habit. Standard automata update cells from neighbors only, ignoring long-range links and tangled wiring real brains use. BraiNCA adds an attention layer picking which messages matter, plus long-range edges and complex topology, while keeping updates local and decentralized. On morphogenesis and motor-control tasks it learned faster and withstood damage better than plain automata, suggesting wiring shape and routing matter most when coordination spans wide space and time.
arxiv-2604-02132: Di Gregorio, Carnevale and Notarstefano lift safety certificates from a reduced model to a full feedback linked system. Many safety critical plants couple slow and fast parts, from robot joints to plants driven by optimization code, yet safety rules often touch only part of the system. Given enough timescale separation, a composite barrier function certifies that the safe set stays invariant for the whole interconnection. The online safety filter then needs only the smaller reduced model. Tests on a robotic arm and an optimization driven plant confirm the approach.
arxiv-2604-02232: Barthel, Hilman and Konovalov classify polynomial functors on spectra through Mackey functors of cross effects. They show multivariable functors match spectral Mackey variants as symmetric monoidal categories, with Day products on both sides. Subdiagonal functors, handled together, admit Mackey accounts step by step with a universal trait. The one variable case gives a new proof of Glasman's result on d-excisive functors, plus a Segal conjecture in Goodwillie theory for prime d.
arxiv-2604-02432: Gonzalez fixes unit errors when a plain time derivative is swapped for a fractional derivative. A simple variable swap, under certain rules, keeps units right for fractional differential equations with non singular kernels. An example shows the method. The short note focuses on the swap itself, showing how a careful variable change keeps units right when these terms enter.
arxiv-2604-02732: Seeyangnok, Pinsook and Ackland study noble-gas impurities in metallic hydrogen at 500 gigapascals, the matter that fills giant planet interiors. Such pressures rule the deep interiors of giant planets. With ab initio molecular dynamics and free-energy math, they find every noble gas costly to place in solid metallic hydrogen. In liquid hydrogen, heavy gases such as argon, krypton, and xenon dissolve, while helium and neon split off. The result gives a micro mechanism for noble-gas fractionation inside giant planets.
arxiv-2604-02932: Moreno-Blazquez, Fele and Alamo build a fast data-driven method to forecast grid frequency from live readings. Their tool rests on kriging interpolation, a statistical method that predicts values from nearby observations, and it exploits the structure of the problem to run in under a second. Accurate frequency forecasts help staff control grids fed by renewables and distributed generation. A simulated distribution grid case study tests the approach.
arxiv-2604-03532: Wong, Sajjad, and Siddique introduce LangFIR, a method that finds language-linked features in sparse autoencoders. It uses only small amounts of single-language data and random-token strings. Random-token strings expose language-free features, so LangFIR filters them out and keeps a sparse set of language-linked features. The features prove very sparse and highly picky, and removing one raises loss only for its language. Steering vectors built from them beat the strongest single-language baseline by up to 4.7 times.
arxiv-2604-03932: Jeremy Alm exhibited finite cyclic group representations for relation algebras 57_65 and 63_65. Of the ten symmetric integral relation algebras on four atoms with at least one flexible atom, all are now known to have finite cyclic representations except 33_65. That last algebra is not even known to be finitely representable at all. The result nearly closes the classification for this family.
arxiv-2604-04332: Barrocas and colleagues present EcoAssist, an energy-aware helper inside a coding editor that reviews AI-written frontend code. Frontend code runs across millions of page views, burning notable energy and feeding digital emissions, yet today's AI coding helpers prize speed over energy impact. EcoAssist estimates each page's energy footprint and suggests targeted optimizations. Across benchmarks of 500 websites it cut per-website energy by 13 to 16 percent on average, raised developer awareness of energy use, and kept productivity intact.
arxiv-2604-04432: Fygenson, Bertini and Padilla show how affordances, the actions a design invites, explain normal distribution plot performance. Past work used affordance theory to explain how design choices affect readers' mental actions. The team studies static normal probability density plots and maps their current affordances. It then finds the best affordances for a common probability-comparison task and builds the Croissant Chart to support them. A preregistered study with 808 people confirms the design shifts task performance predictably, showing affordance-based design can improve visualizations.
arxiv-2604-04532: Mahmood, Abdaljalil and Kurban show that changing an agent judge's language can invert backbone rankings in agentic code benchmarks. Evaluation language usually stays English, but the team localizes the Agent-as-a-Judge prompt stack to English, Arabic, Turkish, Chinese and Hindi. Backbone and language interact: GPT-4o leads in English, while Gemini leads in Arabic at 51.72 percent and Hindi, and no backbone dominates every language. An ablation shows localizing judge-side instructions, not just benchmark content, can prove decisive, with Hindi satisfaction falling sharply under partial localization.
arxiv-2604-04932: Li and five colleagues push detection of machine-written text beyond human-versus-machine labels. Current binary or ternary settings miss the policy gap between human text polished by a model and model text made to sound human. Their RACE method works in a four-class setting, modeling creator and editor as separate roles. It uses Rhetorical Structure Theory to build a logic graph for the creator's base text, then reads discourse units for editor traces. That split sharpens detection.
arxiv-2604-05032: Naik, Sun, and Heyl show neural quantum states as a usable tool for real-time dynamics in three dimensions. Huge complexity limits accurate simulation beyond one dimension, where rapid entanglement growth poses severe challenges. Using a residual convolutional design for cubic spin lattices, they study the three-dimensional transverse-field Ising model. Their states capture well distinct quench regimes, including collapse-and-revival dynamics and dynamics after a sudden quench to the quantum critical point, extending the method to 1000 qubits.
arxiv-2604-05132: Crater and six co-authors investigate how dilution drives joint glassy dynamics in artificial spin ice. Disorder in the energy landscape of magnetic systems has long been known to introduce glassy motion. Yet the role of disorder in driving glass growth remains hard to isolate in materials. Artificial spin ice offers a platform where shape, couplings, and disorder can be built. The authors introduce disorder through random decimation in square spin ice. By taking magnets from random sites, they modify layout and increase strain in the spin network.
arxiv-2604-05232: Silva, de Queiroz, and Schouery present RECORD, a new knapsack and bounded knapsack solver building on COMBO's dynamic programming, weak upper bounds, and surrogate relaxation. RECORD adds multiplicity reduction, on-the-fly aggregation, refined fixing-by-dominance, and a new divisibility bound strengthening fixing and symmetry breaking. These preserve COMBO's near-linear-time behavior on most instances while speeding up challenging cases. Experiments show RECORD beats COMBO and BOUKNAP on difficult benchmarks, often by several orders of magnitude, as a new state-of-the-art solver.
arxiv-2604-05332: Kim and six colleagues catalogue mid-infrared variable sources at the north and south ecliptic poles. They draw on repeated NEOWISE infrared scans across a five-degree circle around each pole. Careful cleaning yields 2764 variables in the north and 27581 in the south. Active galactic nuclei dominate the northern set, while stars dominate the southern one near the Large Magellanic Cloud, and three northern transients all match hidden quasars.
arxiv-2604-05432: Zhang and Pei expose a backdoor attack on tool-using language-model agents that quietly steals stored user context. Their Back-Reveal method plants meaning-based triggers in tuned agents, so a triggered agent pulls private context through memory tools and slips it out inside disguised retrieval calls. Multi-turn chats worsen the leak, as attacker-shaped replies steer later behavior, and the authors call for defenses against exfiltration backdoors.
arxiv-2604-05532: Lee and fourteen colleagues measure hydrogen depletion times inside the stellar discs of 841 gas-rich galaxies from the WALLABY pilot survey. Confining gas and star formation to the disc shortens depletion times by 1.4 billion years on average versus global values. Depletion anti-correlates tightly with stellar surface density, and gas beyond the disc lasts almost 10 billion years longer, marking star formation there as extremely inefficient.
arxiv-2604-05832: Liu and Jansson probe how touchy structured ARX predictors are inside data-driven predictive control. Fitting stays linear, yet the lifted multi-step predictor leans on parameters in a hidden way, muddying error bars and tuning. Their first-order straightening yields a control-ready error term and a tuning gauge for kernel shaping, best when excitation runs weak.
arxiv-2604-06032: Franzen and Pourkamali-Anaraki's 2026 paper tackles uncertainty in neural network classifiers. Their softmax scores give no built-in trust measure and swing across training runs. Instead of fragile evidential training, they estimate Dirichlet parameters from ensembles of softmax outputs. They use a method-of-moments estimator, with an optional maximum-likelihood refinement. The build separates uncertainty work from touchy loss design and steadies single-run swings. Across several datasets, the ensemble-derived estimates improve confidence scores and selective classification, where a model holds back on shaky calls.
arxiv-2604-06232: Atzenhofer-Baumgartner and Kowald study scholars using digital archives, where standard recommender ideas break down. From focus groups and interviews with 18 researchers, they find four points of divergence. First, context volatility: tastes shift with tasks and skill. Second, epistemic trust: relevance hinges on origins. Third, contrastive seeking: scholars want items that challenge them. Fourth, strand continuity: research follows long threads, not short sessions. The authors offer these dimensions as a diagnostic framework for archives and similar domains.
arxiv-2604-06632: Pinedo and Frolov construct static, spherically symmetric black holes in quasi-topological gravity joined to Born-Infeld nonlinear electrodynamics. From the reduced action they derive closed-form expressions for the electric field, the nonlinear Lagrangian, and the metric function, the last involving hypergeometric functions. In some models where vacuum holes stay regular, charged holes grow a curvature singularity at a finite interior radius. In Born-Infeld-type models holes stay regular, but the neutral solution's de Sitter core gives way to an anti-de Sitter core.
arxiv-2604-07432: Nastase, Nunez, and Roychowdhury study Krylov complexity in holography for probes with inner structure and for spread-out probes. A heavy charged particle in AdS5 times S5 shows how inner motion changes complexity growth, giving a symmetry-resolved case. Baryon-vertex and giant-graviton probes keep the expected leading large-time form, with telling subleading effects from structure and charges. A falling string stretched along space differs in subleading and middle regimes, showing spread-out probes carry finer spread complexity.
arxiv-2604-07532: Turgut proposes IPEK, an event-stakes-aware trust framework for vehicular networks facing shrewd insider bad actors. Such actors report trivial events honestly to build standing, fake safety-critical reports, and corrupt feedback about other vehicles. IPEK scales rewards and fines with event gravity and location stakes, discounts feedback straying by habit from witness view, and fuses feedback with Dempster-Shafer global trust using Yager rule. In tests with up to 25 percent bad actors, IPEK beats both rivals on F1 score under all attacks.
arxiv-2604-07732: Cai and four colleagues examine how independent developers building for Twitch seek and offer help in a Discord community when the platform itself answers slowly. Topic modeling plus close qualitative reading show their questions about social, technical, and policy matters lean heavily on Twitch, a dependence the authors read as platform labor. Shuttling between Discord and Twitch deepens that burden, and the community survives through flexible roles that bridge the two spaces.
arxiv-2604-07832: Álvarez, Martínez Alonso, and Medina study how the classical Szegő curve deforms, viewed through three lenses at once. An electrostatic equilibrium problem, a dual hydrodynamic model, and a random matrix model all rest on the same limiting distribution of zeros of scaled Laguerre polynomials. The deformation parameter tracks how fast a sequence approaches the negative integers. The team shows the Schwarz functions of these curves can be written with the Lambert W function, and they analyze the Stahl-Gonchar S-property in that formulation.
arxiv-2604-07932: Han and 64 colleagues analyze ten binary-lens microlensing events from the 2023 to 2025 seasons as candidate hosts of brown-dwarf companions. For each event they model the light curve, explore degeneracies, and, where finite-source effects appear, measure the angular Einstein radius. The event OGLE-2023-BLG-0249 additionally yields a microlens parallax, giving lens masses and distance directly. Remaining events gain physical properties through Bayesian analyses with Galactic priors. The resulting sample sharpens the census of brown dwarfs in binary lens systems.
arxiv-2604-08432: Calçado, Turitsyn, and Manuylovich build tiny photonic neural networks entirely from standard telecom parts, dodging the usual optical to electrical conversions. Each link carries a trainable nonlinear unit built from an interferometer, an optical amplifier, and variable attenuators. A four module network hit 94.3 percent on nonlinear classification tests, near software results with far fewer weights, and held up well under realistic hardware noise.
arxiv-2604-08532: Nan Huang and six colleagues improve 4D perception without any labeled data, using unlabeled video to keep teaching pretrained multi view reconstruction models. Their SelfEvo framework distills a model against itself through spatiotemporal context asymmetry, studying which loss signals and asymmetry forms make self teaching work. Across eight benchmarks it improves baselines and transfers across base models, gaining up to 36.5 percent on video depth with strong gains on camera estimation too.
arxiv-2604-08832: Hirabayashi and colleagues survey the Hayabusa2 long mission flyby of near Earth rock Torifune, planned for July 2026. After bringing back Ryugu samples in December 2020, the craft began a decade long mission. It spans alien planet and dust watches, the flyby, and a 2031 meeting with rock 1998 KY26. The flyby will pass about 1 to 10 km from the center of Torifune at 5.25 km per second, fixing pointing for high detail imaging. It will probe inner solar system matter transport and world defense.
arxiv-2604-09632: Rahman and four colleagues predict 5G downlink performance from live measurements on ordinary smartphones. Their platform pairs the srsRAN 5G stack on a Dell desktop base station, operating at 3.4 GHz, with two Pixel 7a phones recording channel quality, modulation and coding scheme, bit rate, timing intervals, and block error rate. Traffic comes from Ookla servers worldwide, iperf flows, and YouTube sessions, under line-of-sight and blocked conditions, stationary and moving. Five supervised regression models are tested, and throughput and block error rate prove accurately predictable from commercial hardware.
arxiv-2604-10032: Zhang, Cheng, Wang, and Liu remove unwanted concepts from generative models with a closed-form linear method instead of iterative training. A proxy projection first isolates the target concept, then a constrained transform acts within the left null space of known concept directions, leaving other concepts intact. The approach matches or beats leading methods on object and style removal in Stable Diffusion variants and FLUX while preserving unrelated concepts, and it applies in seconds.
arxiv-2604-10132: Tan and eight colleagues define Semantic Manipulation Localization, a task that finds subtle edits changing what an image means. Modern editing leaves few low-level artifacts, tweaking an object's traits, state, or links while matching surroundings. Standard tools miss these edits, since they lean on artifacts, not meaning. The team builds a benchmark with pixel annotations from a meaning-driven editing pipeline. Their TRACE framework reasons in three stages: anchoring, perturbation sensing, and meaning-constrained reasoning. TRACE beats existing methods on the benchmark with more complete and coherent results.
arxiv-2604-10432: Hu and six colleagues teach robots to drop items into exact slots from spoken orders. Flat vision language action nets fumble fine placement under layered word commands. Their AnySlot system first paints a visual mark on the target slot, then steers by that mark. Splitting slot choice from low level control lifts both word sense and spatial care. A new nine part test set, SlotBench, shows clear wins over flat and modular rivals in fresh tasks.
arxiv-2604-10532: Wang and 52 colleagues review the second NTIRE face restoration contest. The task prizes natural looks that keep the same face, with no caps on compute or training data. Scores blend image quality with an AdaFace identity check. Of 96 entrants, 10 teams filed valid models and 9 reached the final board. The review maps the top tricks and trends shaping real world face repair.
arxiv-2604-10632: Spanio, Frezzato, and Rodà test whether sound-taste links survive when a small listener-annotated collection is scaled up automatically. Such links appear in museum and food-tourism exhibits. They grow 257 annotated tracks into 49,300 labeled segments from the Free Music Archive. They check the patterns against food-chemistry profiles for 20 largely Italian dishes, rated by 49 listeners. The patterns carry over across every taste dimension. Listener ratings match the computed profiles well beyond chance.
arxiv-2604-10732: The CMS team searches proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV for microscopic black holes, string balls, and electroweak sphalerons, using 138 inverse femtobarns. Two data-driven plans set model-free limits on multi-object states and model-based limits on black hole production. In large-extra-dimension models, semiclassical black holes below eight point four to eleven point four TeV and string balls below nine to ten point seven are excluded at 95 percent confidence, extending reach. A search caps the share of high-energy quark-quark interactions yielding such a transition.
arxiv-2604-10832: Dhakar, Sinha, and Sural show how organizational privacy policies can be checked against privacy law using APLiance, an attribute-based access control framework for policy-law compliance. The method models law sections as access rules and policy clauses as sequences of implied access requests; a policy complies when its requests are permitted by the corresponding rules. Demonstrated on India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the approach is general to any policy-law setting. A browser plugin for real-time compliance checking on website privacy pages has been publicly released.
arxiv-2604-10932: Samsonau argues science should open its process, not its outputs. Current practice shows conclusions but hides their making: private work, polished papers, errors punished by retraction, not amendment. Two decades of reform opened papers, data, code, notebooks, and protocols, yet the unit stayed finished, never the thinking process: shifting questions, dead ends, and shifts. Opening the process would speed progress, widen access, raise trust, and scale quality checks. The workflow needs visible, trackable, forkable work, with changes recorded, and branching open from any point.
arxiv-2604-11032: Xu and Shi model plasma lensing of substructures on pulsar scintillation screens. Radio pulsars are highly steady point sources that probe the ionized medium between stars. Observations show flipped arclets on the second spectrum, showing near-linear aligned images from screen substructures. Their shapes remain unknown yet crucial to their real nature. Using three lens models, the authors find which traits data can constrain. The outer caustic is the clearest feature, seen via multi-epoch or wideband data, and its place constrains the maximum column density gradient.
arxiv-2604-11432: Piarulli and nine colleagues test congestion across modern supercomputer nets. They cover EDR, HDR, and NDR InfiniBand, Cray Slingshot, and new Ethernet fabrics. Tests span steady congestion and varied bursty patterns from AI workloads, at many system scales. The study maps how congestion shows up differently as systems grow and how it degrades group communication. As more users share bigger machines, such tests set real speed expectations. The overview aims to guide congestion and load-balancing design for researchers and HPC architects.
arxiv-2604-11632: Wei and seven colleagues introduce CArtBench, a museum-grounded benchmark for vision-language models on Chinese artworks beyond short QA. Built from Palace Museum objects aligned with catalog pages across five categories and multiple dynasties, it holds four subtasks. They cover evidence-grounded recognition, expert-style appreciation, reinterpretation with expert ratings, and authenticity tests under similar-looking confounds. Across nine models, high accuracy masks sharp drops on hard evidence linking and style-to-period inference. Long-form appreciation trails experts, and authenticity discrimination stays near chance.
arxiv-2604-12032: Gómez-Valent, Zheng, and Amendola test coupled dark energy: cold dark matter interacts with a spin-0 field through a field-dependent mass. An ultra-light scalar mediates a fifth force. Using Planck, DESI, and supernovae, they compare a flat potential with a Peebles-Ratra potential. The flat case ignores the coupling sign; the Peebles-Ratra case breaks that symmetry late, with no important fitting asymmetry. All cases peak near 0.03, excluding no coupling at 95 percent confidence at most, and explain a phantom-divide crossing within two-sigma bands.
arxiv-2604-12132: LHeureux and six colleagues sort cloudy from clear atmospheres among ultracool dwarfs using synthetic JWST mid-infrared photometry built from Spitzer spectra of 113 objects. Diagrams pairing two filters best separate L dwarfs carrying silicate clouds, and objects below a small color threshold prove seven times likelier to be cloudy. Their work shows such photometry can pick cloudy targets for follow-up spectra, saving telescope time.
arxiv-2604-12232: Shen and five colleagues introduce TEMPLATEFUZZ, a fuzzing framework that attacks language models through chat templates rather than prompt wording alone. Element-level mutations generate template variants, heuristic search steers generation toward higher attack success while preserving accuracy, and active learning builds a light rule-based oracle for jailbreak judging. Across twelve open models it averages 98.2 percent attack success with only 1.1 percent accuracy loss, and reaches 90 percent on five commercial models.
arxiv-2604-12432: Matthias Kunik builds a fresh model theory for formal systems of mathematics. Such systems use precise symbolic rules to frame mathematical reasoning. He introduces isomorphic and homomorphic structures for formal languages. The paper presents results and examples for those structures. It closes by discussing reduced set theory, RST, adapted to the new theory. The theory extends work from an earlier paper by the author.
arxiv-2604-12732: W. S. Oliveira and two colleagues study quantum percolation on a honeycomb lattice. Site dilution and random spin-orbit coupling shape the system. Exact solutions plus size scaling track the metal-insulator switch. Without spin-orbit coupling, the quantum threshold stays finite and beats the classical threshold. Spectra cross from orthogonal to symplectic types. The quantum threshold shifts lower, favoring spread. Strong coupling saturates the threshold, while the exponent nears the symplectic class value.
arxiv-2604-12832: Iman Islam and three colleagues catch and fix faulty labels while training heart ultrasound segmentation models. Manual labels carry random errors and systematic biases. On the CAMUS set, three error types are simulated. A Variance of Gradients method flags bad labels far better than a loss-based method. A pseudo-labeling step refurbishes suspect labels. A standard U-Net still holds up under random errors and moderate systematic errors up to 50 percent. Detection plus refurbishment helps most when errors run high.
arxiv-2604-12932: Andrei Pantea and five colleagues make turbulent particle-pair paths with diffusion models. Diffusion models already make single-particle Lagrangian paths in turbulent flows. The team extends the method to joint pairs of velocity paths. Made pairs match separation shifts, including departures from Richardson scaling. Single-particle statistics from earlier studies stay intact. The result is a data-driven picture of pair dispersion for fluid dynamics and beyond.
arxiv-2604-13232: Phan-Tat, Heylen, Geeraerts, De Pascale, and Speelmana re-examine SemEval-2020 Task 1, the leading shared benchmark for lexical semantic change detection, through operationalization, data quality, and benchmark design. They argue its discrete-sense framing misses gradual, constructional, collocational, and discourse-level change, while annotation choices and thresholds limit validity. Data problems include OCR noise, malformed characters, truncated sentences, inconsistent lemmatization, and tagging errors, and small curated target sets with narrow language coverage reduce realism.
arxiv-2604-13832: Tan and five colleagues study closed orbits in a Schwarzschild spacetime inside a Dehnen-type dark matter halo. Solving the geodesic equations, they map strictly closed timelike orbits and simulate their gravitational waves and light curves. Orbit shape depends mainly on the ratio of azimuthal to radial period. Halo core scale and density enlarge the orbital scale, causing a phase lag in gravitational-wave signals. In one parameter space, light-curve peak counts relate linearly to orbital leaf counts, offering multimessenger signatures of the dark matter environment.
arxiv-2604-14032: Malik pairs a high-level reinforcement learning policy with a deterministic runtime safety shield for power-grid operation. The policy proposes abstract actions while the shield filters unsafe ones through fast forward simulation, enforcing safety as a runtime invariant regardless of policy quality. On Grid2Op stress tests and zero-shot deployment on a large 2021 transmission grid, the hierarchy survives longer with lower peak loading than flat or safety-only methods.
arxiv-2604-14332: De equates diffusion-model inference with overdamped Langevin motion, so a substrate holding the score function settles to the right output by thermodynamics alone. Two barriers blocked scale-up: non-local skip connections, which analog bases cannot show, and input conditioning with far too little signal. Hierarchical bilinear coupling turns U-Net skip connections into rank-k interactions from Gram matrices, using far fewer links. A 2,560-parameter digital interface overcomes conditioning, and the full system reaches 0.9906 decoder cosine similarity with roughly ten-million-fold energy savings over GPU inference.
arxiv-2604-14432: Kunzler, Bruk, Kaiser, and Gurka combine stereolithography with tailored fiber placement to print shape-memory-alloy hybrid composites in a fully additive process. Alloy wires fixed to a textile layer sit inside a UV-cured polymer matrix under a re-entrant honeycomb top layer, and the three-layer stack bends out of plane when heated. Eight geometric variants were built and measured optically, testing manual embedding against automated placement. Automated placement wins on reproducibility and symmetric bending, and the honeycomb tuning of stiffness points toward programmable morphing structures.
arxiv-2604-14932: Chen and 11 others propose WavAlign, an adaptive post-training recipe for spoken dialogue models. Direct preference optimization fails here because sparse preference signals clash with dense speech output under shared updates. Their recipe constrains preference updates to the semantic channel, improves sound behavior with explicit anchors, and tunes the mixture from rollout statistics to avoid bad gradients. Tests across spoken dialogue benchmarks and model designs show consistent gains in semantic quality and speech expressiveness.
arxiv-2604-15132: Bergner, Hanada, and Mendicelli present a minimal digital-quantum implementation of pure SU(N) Yang-Mills theory in 3+1 dimensions. Built on an orbifold lattice protocol with logarithmic scaling in Hilbert-space truncation, it adds simpler Hamiltonians and faster convergence to the infinite-mass limit. For SU(2), embedding the group as a 3-sphere in four-dimensional space cuts resources further. Monte Carlo benchmarks support the approach as a practical route toward quantum advantage.
arxiv-2604-15532: Vakhnovskyi presents a dual-radio mesh for emergency communication without infrastructure, pairing BLE clusters with a LoRa backbone. Local clusters route over BLE advertising-based AODV, while elected cluster heads bridge traffic over LoRa. With locality bias at or above 0.76, 82 to 90 percent of traffic stays on BLE, cutting LoRa energy use by 79 percent versus LoRa-only mesh, with 10-kilometer-plus reach and sub-50-millisecond intra-cluster latency.
arxiv-2604-15732: Yoshimura, van de Beek, and Chiba argue that in long-context LLM serving, right answers are speed, since wrong answers force retries that pile up user-seen lag. They coin Time-to-Correct-Answer, the wall-clock span to the first right reply. Prompt length and tongue widen right-answer spread, swelling that span. Their Lightweight Accuracy-Aware Routing steers asks by skill, cutting that span, so right-answer skill earns rank as a first-class systems goal.
arxiv-2604-15832: Ratcliffe and Nguyen investigate which positive integers up to 10,000 can be written as a difference of two rational fourth powers. The work follows Cohen's study of sums of two rational fourth powers in his Number Theory volume, which covered the equation with a plus sign. For the difference equation, the authors obtain the complete list of positive integers up to 10,000 representable in this form with nonzero rational numbers.
arxiv-2604-16032: Gerd Röpke derives plasma thermal and transport properties from quantum statistics as equilibrium correlation functions. These can be worked out by hand or by code, including DFT-MD or PIMC simulations. Virial expansions from the Green's function method benchmark numeric runs and help at low density. Equation-of-state results cover the uniform electron gas and hydrogen plasma. The dielectric function is covered, with direct current flow as a special case. Cases show where further work is needed for a full picture of hot, dense plasmas.
arxiv-2604-16132: Zhu and five colleagues assess open-source language models that code interviews by theme, with 21 Black men who survived local firearm violence. Manual theme study and coding are slow and labor-heavy, spurring auto coding. Some model setups spot key codes, but overall fit stays low and swings with data handling.
